key_insight: Naive Bayes and linear SVM achieved perfect held-out accuracy on a small Ghanaian mobile-money SMS corpus, showing promise for scam detection.
engineering_relevance: Classical text classifiers offer a lightweight approach to carrier- or handset-level scam filtering in resource-constrained settings.
method: Normalise currency amounts, phone numbers, and USSD codes.
Encode SMS text with TF-IDF unigrams and bigrams.
Compare Multinomial Naive Bayes, linear SVM, and Random Forest.
evidence_signal: Across 220 labelled messages in 18 subcategories, stratified five-fold cross-validation yielded mean accuracies of 96.6% for Naive Bayes, 94.9% for SVM, and 92.0% for Random Forest; Naive Bayes and SVM reached 1.00 accuracy, F1, and AUC on a 20% held-out test set.
watch_item: The small, template-based corpus may inflate performance; validate on larger, naturalistic multilingual messages before deployment.
paper_title: Machine Learning-Based Detection of Mobile Money Scan Messages in Ghana: A Comparative Evaluation of Naive Bayes, Support Vector Machine, and Randon Forest Classifiers
